question: Screen for stocks trading below their sector's average P/E but with ROE above the sector average — cheap relative to peers yet more profitable. Restrict to US large caps.

_conventions._note: For the fields below, read the `definition` and/or `sign` before interpreting the value — a negative can MEAN something (an outflow, a benefit) and an ambiguous name needs its definition. Every other field is a plain magnitude.

eps_diluted.definition: PER SHARE, in the company's REPORTING currency (NOT USD-normalized like the _usd fields) — don't mix it with the USD amounts.

_pagination.note: Over-fetched ~4× your intended show (15) as a look-ahead buffer so 'a few more' is served from these 41 rows — do NOT re-screen for a few more. This is the COMPLETE match set — `count` is the exact total.

answer_to_user: US large-cap, each stock judged against ITS OWN sector cohort (vs_cohort own=true): P/E below the sector average AND ROE above the sector average — intersected. 41 matches from a 126-stock US-large-cap universe. Each row shows its own cohort benchmark, e.g. NVIDIA P/E 33.7 vs its sector avg 41.7 (cheaper) and ROE 82% vs sector avg 36% (more profitable). Other hits: Apple, Alphabet, Eli Lilly, Micron, JPMorgan, J&J, Oracle. Peer-relative on both legs, not fixed thresholds.
